steps: First holder obtains monotonically increasing token 41.
It pauses long enough for ownership to expire.
New holder obtains token 42 and begins protected work.
Resource remembers 42 and rejects delayed writes carrying stale token 41.

lesson.scenario: A storage writer rejects a paused former lock holder by checking monotonic tokens at the protected resource.

steps.narration: The lock transaction stores owner=A, expiry=13:04:30Z,token=41 after the linearizable counter increments.

steps.narration: Storage compares 41 with highestToken=0, raises the fence to 41, and appends the mutation.

action: Acquire expired lock and allocate token 42

steps.title: Reject the stale delayed write
steps.narration: A resumes and sends a buffered write, but Storage compares 41 below the current ownership token 42 supplied by B acquisition and rejects it before mutation.
steps.outcome: A stale process cannot corrupt the new owner work.

steps.title: Commit only the newer owner
steps.narration: Storage accepts token 42, appends checkpoint 901, and keeps highestToken=42 for every later comparison.
steps.outcome: Ownership overlap in process memory cannot produce out-of-generation writes.

production.scenario: Stripe payout exports must prevent a stale job owner from writing a second settlement file after failover.
components: global finance workflows creating settlement batches that need exclusive export ownership
service boundary that starts export jobs and hands workers their current ownership token
control-plane service that issues monotonically increasing write generations for fenced ownership
durable authority in PostgreSQL for export owner, generation, and final artifact pointers
produces bank-bound files only when carrying the newest accepted generation
control path that promotes a new owner after worker death and retires stale generations
observability path for stale-write rejections, ownership churn, and export completion
flows: Finance workflows request exclusive ownership before producing a settlement artifact.
The boundary asks the fencing service for the next valid generation for that export batch.
The ownership ledger records the accepted generation as the durable authority for future writes.
Only workers carrying the latest token may write the settlement file or mark it complete.
Failover control requests a newer generation when the active writer stops renewing.
The authoritative ledger reveals stale completion attempts that must be ignored or rolled back.
Operators monitor stale-write rejection rate, takeover latency, and export success.
